job.title: Advancement Programs Director
job.description:
• Leading global university 
  • Shape the future of alumni and donor engagement
  • Build loyalty at scale


About the organisation

UNSW Sydney is a globally connected university with more than 400,000 alumni and a donor community of approximately 50,000. Its strategy, Progress for All, sets an ambitious agenda for creating positive societal impact through education, research and meaningful engagement with its communities and partners. Following a refreshed Advancement strategy, UNSW has created this new role to bring greater strategic coherence to how it engages alumni, donors and supporters throughout their relationship with the University. This is an opportunity to help shape the next phase of an ambitious Advancement function at one of Australia’s leading universities, applying contemporary thinking in loyalty, customer experience, data and lifecycle engagement to a purpose-led organisation with significant scale and impact.


About the role

Reporting to the Chief Advancement Officer, and leading a team, the Advancement Programs Director is a key member of the Advancement leadership team, working alongside the Directors of Development, Alumni Experience and Advancement Services to shape a more connected and insight-led approach to alumni and donor engagement. 

The Director will provide strategic leadership for supporter journeys, lifecycle engagement and development communications, including community giving. A central focus will be understanding how different audiences move through the advancement ecosystem, from alumni engagement and community giving through to major and principal gifts, and designing more connected, purposeful experiences along the journey. 

The role will establish the strategies, frameworks and standards that enable consistent communications, events, stewardship and supporter experiences. Working in partnership with Advancement Services, the Director will define the segmentation, data, reporting and insights required to understand audience behaviour, evaluate performance and improvement engagement over time. 

The Director will also represent Advancement audiences and priorities to central marketing, digital and communications teams and senior University leaders. A key early priority will be developing a clear first-year strategy that maps audiences and cohorts, identifies the journeys and experiences required, establishes clear priorities and makes a compelling case for future investment.


About you

Tertiary qualified, you are a senior customer, marketing, or engagement leader with deep expertise in lifecycle strategy, loyalty or CRM-driven engagement, gained in complex organisations. Higher education or philanthropy experience is not essential. You understand how data, insight and customer behaviour can be translated into more meaningful engagement and measurable results. You bring a strong point of view on best practice, can distinguish between what is strategically important and what is simply possible, and are confident setting priorities, including being clear about what not to pursue. You have experience leading multidisciplinary teams and influencing across marketing, digital and data specialists while bringing stakeholders with you through change. You are comfortable operating across a complex institution, building a case for investment and translating strategy into practical action.

You bring curiosity and commercial judgement, along with the confidence to build something new in an environment where ambiguity, competing priorities and limited resources are part of the landscape. What matters is your ability to understand audiences, connect data and experience, build effective strategies and create the conditions for long-term engagement.

Most importantly, you will be excited by the opportunity to build something new and establish the foundations for more connected alumni and donor engagement at scale. 


How to apply

Click ‘Apply’ to submit your CV along with a covering letter. For more information prior to application, please contact Kylie Kilmartin at SHK on 0401 167 433 or via email at kylie.kilmartin@shk.com.au. Direct and third-party applications will be forwarded to SHK.

Zoos Victoria is a world-leading conservation organisation and Victorian Government statutory authority operating Melbourne Zoo, Werribee Open Range Zoo, Healesville Sanctuary and Kyabram Fauna Park. Welcoming more than three million visitors annually, a paid membership base of over 390,000 and caring for over 5,500 animals, the organisation combines a powerful conservation mission with significant commercial scale and community impact. The Head will develop and maintain the Digital and AI Strategy and is accountable for the Information and Data Protection Framework, cybersecurity, and the reliability of internal and external applications. This includes developing data governance policies, a centralised data management framework, and data literacy across key functional areas to support evidence-based decision making. The Head will also lead business application projects with effective change management, manage functional budgets, and lead a team of 12 (five direct reports) across all four properties. Key to success will be securing ownership of the strategy from the Board, Senior Executive and staff, and making sure initiatives are delivered in a coordinated way with minimal disruption.

 

 About you

You have led accomplished digital and/or IT teams, coached managers to influence stakeholders, and driven organisational change without creating silos. Your background in data analytics, performance reporting and performance measurement supports both operational objectives and the monitoring of strategy. job.title: Chief Information Officer

  • Statewide 24/7 emergency healthcare
  • Enabling best care for Victorians


About the organisation

Ambulance Victoria (AV) brings patient-focused, out-of-hospital, mobile and emergency healthcare to the Victorian community. Operating 24/7 across Metropolitan Melbourne and Regional Victoria, the organisation depends on a secure and resilient technology environment to support its frontline services. AV's Patient Care Commitment is to provide care that is caring, safe, effective and connected for every patient, every time, underpinned by the values of care, accountability, respect and excellence. Within this organisation, technology is positioned as a strategic enabler of service reform, innovation and improved organisational performance.


About the role

Reporting to the Executive Director Enterprise Services, the Chief Information Officer (CIO) holds enterprise-wide accountability for AV's technology, digital and data enablement strategy, and for the performance, security and resilience of its technology environment. The CIO will lead the evolution of a secure, integrated and contemporary technology ecosystem, driving digital transformation, technology modernisation and service improvement across the organisation. This includes technology strategy and architecture, IT service delivery, cyber security, data and AI enablement, and portfolio, investment and vendor management. Working in partnership with clinical, operational and corporate leaders, the CIO will translate organisational priorities into digital capabilities. These will see a modernisation of services, increased interoperability with health, emergency services and government partners, and improved patient outcomes and employee experience. Key to success will be leading organisational and cultural change, ensuring technology investment delivers measurable value, and providing authoritative advice to the CEO, Executive Leadership Team and Board.


About you

You are a commercially astute technology executive with experience leading a large-scale, complex technology function within a highly operational, service-based or similarly multifaceted organisation. Experience in government, health, emergency services, critical infrastructure or another heavily regulated environment will be well regarded. You have led large scale digital and technology transformation and bring strong commercial capability across operating and capital budgets, strategic sourcing, contract negotiation and the management of outsourced and managed services. An inspiring people leader, you build high-performing, accountable and service-oriented teams, and foster a culture in which people constructively challenge existing practices and take accountability for outcomes. Your understanding of cyber security, data, AI and emerging technology, combined with sound strategic judgement, allows you to advise and influence boards and executive leaders on significant technology and investment matters. Tertiary qualified in information technology, computer science, information systems, business or a related discipline (postgraduate qualifications well received), you recognise this a rare opportunity to have state-wide impact.

A substantial fundraising operation, underpinned by a high-performing transformational giving team, has delivered consistent year-on-year growth and continues to play a critical role in advancing the organisation’s purpose. Through an integrated and holistic approach, it creates lasting spiritual and social change for individuals and families across Australia.


About the role

Reporting to the General Manager, Transformational Gifts, the Manager, Philanthropy plays a critical leadership role in advancing the organisation’s mission through the development of meaningful, high-value philanthropic relationships in line with the fundraising strategy. This position is responsible for driving sustainable income growth by identifying, cultivating, soliciting and stewarding major donors including securing seven-figure gifts, and building strong, long-term relationships with philanthropic stakeholders. Combining strategic thinking with hands-on relationship management, the appointee will ensure that philanthropic investment is aligned with organisational priorities and delivers measurable social impact. Collaborating with internal stakeholders to translate programmatic needs into compelling funding propositions, the appointee will build long-term partnerships grounded in trust, transparency and shared purpose, and through disciplined pipeline management, strong market intelligence, and exceptional donor engagement, contribute, to revenue diversification, multi-year funding security, and the overall growth of the philanthropy portfolio. The role is also responsible for achieving financial and non-financial targets, inspiring a national team that is tasked with acquiring new strategic relationships, and driving revenue growth and retention. Critical to success is building team capabilities and optimising ROI performance, while ensuring contemporary best practice processes. 


About you

You are an experienced philanthropy or major gifts leader with demonstrable experience securing seven-figure gifts. You bring leadership experience, ideally across a geographically dispersed team, and possess the commercial and strategic capability to manage a multi ten-million-dollar portfolio of philanthropic revenue. Your stakeholder management skills are well developed, and you present with the gravitas and executive presence required to engage ultra-high-net-worth individuals and their intermediaries. You have the ability to navigate a large complex organisation and to work collaboratively and collectively with this framework. You may come from a large charity, higher education, health or medical research, other relevant philanthropic sectors, or a high-net-worth relationship management background in wealth or private banking where your skills translate meaningfully into the welfare sector. You thrive on operating within a values-led, mission-driven organisation where you can meaningfully impact and transform people’s lives.
